entries.title: SEC Corporation Finance staff issues FAQs on crypto asset classification and investment contract analysis
entries.facts: The SEC's Division of Corporation Finance has published a set of staff frequently asked questions stamped "Sept. 25, 2026", titled "Frequently Asked Questions on the Application of the Federal Securities Laws to Certain Types of Crypto Assets and Certain Transactions Involving Crypto Assets". The page states that the answers "represent the views of the staff of the Division of Corporation Finance" and "are not a rule, regulation or statement of the Securities and Exchange Commission". The FAQs are organized in two groups. The first group, on classification of crypto assets, addresses how the definitions of "functional" and "decentralized" relate to an issuer's representations, how Staking Receipt Tokens are classified, and what distinguishes a "receipt" from other financial instruments. The second group, on crypto assets subject to investment contracts, addresses when promotional communications constitute representations of essential managerial efforts, whether a non-security crypto asset ceases to be an investment contract when representations are assumed by another party, what activities do not constitute essential managerial efforts after a crypto system is functional, whether issuer statements can create new investment contracts for functional and decentralized systems, whether buyback program announcements constitute essential managerial effort representations, and whether a trading platform offering a secondary market qualifies as a promoter. No SEC press release accompanied the FAQs.
entries.source_label: SEC Division of Corporation Finance staff FAQs (sec.gov), dated Sept. 25, 2026
entries.relevant_to: token issuers, staking service providers, crypto trading platforms, securities counsel

entries.issuing_body: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
entries.title: Both Federal Reserve GENIUS Act stablecoin proposals are now published in the Federal Register, with a 120-day application clock and a deemed-approval default
entries.facts: Two Federal Reserve proposed rules implementing the GENIUS Act published in the Federal Register on September 29, 2026. Document 2026-19860, "Implementing the Federal Reserve Board's Responsibilities Under the GENIUS Act", carries RIN 7100-AH29 and Docket R-1899 and would affect 12 CFR parts 208, 211, 217, 225, 247 and 263. Its DATES section reads "Comments must be received by November 30, 2026." Its summary states that the Board "proposes to issue regulations to implement the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act) with respect to Board-supervised permitted payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs) and certain other entities that are subject to the Board's jurisdiction", and that the Board "proposes to issue regulations to implement the prohibition on tying in section 4(a)(8) of the GENIUS Act, which is applicable generally to all PPSIs." Document 2026-19899, "Application Procedures for Board-Supervised Insured Depository Institutions Seeking Approval for a Subsidiary To Issue Payment Stablecoins", carries RIN 7100-AH30 and Docket R-1900 and would affect 12 CFR parts 247 and 262. Its DATES section reads "Comments must be received by the Board on or before November 30, 2026." On the application timetable, that document states that "not later than 30 days after receiving an application, the Board must notify the applicant as to whether the Board considers the application to be substantially complete"; that "the Board shall render a decision on the application not later than 120 days after the submission date"; and that "if the Board fails to render a decision on a complete application within 120 days of the submission date, the application shall be deemed approved." A denied applicant may request a hearing "not later than 30 days after the applicant receives notice of the denial", the Board notices the time and place "[n]ot later than 30 days after the date of receipt of the request", and "[n]ot later than 60 days after the date of that hearing, the Board shall notify the applicant of a final determination."
entries.source_label: Federal Register documents 2026-19899 and 2026-19860, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, proposed rules published Sept. 29, 2026
entries.relevant_to: payment stablecoin issuers, state member banks, bank holding companies, reserve custodians

entries.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury, on behalf of the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee
entries.title: Treasury stablecoin certification rule will be effective on publication, but certifications will not be accepted until Paperwork Reduction Act approval
entries.facts: Treasury's interim final rule "Forms and Procedures for Review of State Certifications by the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee", Federal Register document 2026-19966 at RIN 1505-AC97 and docket TREAS-DO-2026-0562, states in its DATES section: "Effective date: This interim final rule is effective [INSERT DATE OF PUBLICATION IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER]; however, certifications will not be accepted until after Paperwork Reduction Act approval of the information collection. Treasury will post a notification on its website as to when certifications will be accepted. Comment date: Comments on this interim final rule must be received on or before [INSERT DATE 60 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER]." Its summary states that Treasury "is issuing this interim final rule on behalf of the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee", that the Committee "is adopting interim procedural regulations and forms to implement its responsibilities under section 4(c)" of the GENIUS Act, and that the regulations "set out a process to facilitate the Committee's approval or denial of certifications submitted by State payment stablecoin regulators under section 4(c)(4) of the GENIUS Act, and prescribe the form of such certifications." Both bracketed dates were still unfilled when this entry was written, and the document had not yet appeared in a published Federal Register issue.
entries.source_label: Federal Register public inspection, unpublished document 2026-19966, Department of the Treasury interim final rule filed Sept. 29, 2026
entries.relevant_to: state payment stablecoin regulators, payment stablecoin issuers using the state pathway
